name: Hex Chess
tagline: Chess on a hexagonal board. The computer thinks here, or a friend from one link.
description:
A hexagonal board — the kind with three bishops — and no game server. The computer thinks on this device, or you send one link and a friend sits the other colour. There is no account.

White and black take turns on ninety-one hexes. Each side has a king, a queen, two rooks, two knights, three bishops (one for each colour of hex), and nine pawns. Tap a piece, then tap a hex. Legal hexes light up.

On your own you play a computer that looks a little way ahead, right here on the phone or computer. Pass the device for two people in the same room, or press Play a friend and send the invite: the same board, live, on two devices.

There is no castling. A pawn that steps two hexes can still be taken in passing. Close the tab and the game is still in the icon — the file is the save.

This is the hexagonal kind, not the square board.
